land.text: Daimabad and Inamgaon, sites of both cultures; 'The Jorwe culture was preceded by the Malwa culture'

correction.text: 'existed in large areas of the Deccan region in what is now Maharashtra state', 'over 200 settlements' (Jorwe, Daimabad, Inamgaon, Prakashe, Walki in Pune district), drawn as discs on Ahmednagar, Pune, Nashik, Dhule, Aurangabad, Sholapur and Burhanpur; in -1300 'also reached north into the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh' (Navdatoli near Maheshwar)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). 'The early phase of the culture is dated to c. 1400-1000 BCE, while the late phase is dated to c. 1000-700 BCE.' The page gives no area; the Maharashtra discs resolve to about 136,000 km2, much less than the whole state (the Konkan coast and Vidarbha are left out because no site is named there).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The culture 'also reached north into the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh'; with the Malwa plateau the shape resolves to about 291,000 km2. 'Most Jorwe culture sites were abandoned around 1000 BCE, possibly due to famine or drought'; the page names no region for the contraction, so the shape is kept to -700.

region.text: 'existed in large areas of the Deccan region in what is now Maharashtra state', 'over 200 settlements' (Jorwe, Daimabad, Inamgaon, Prakashe, Walki in Pune district), drawn as discs on Ahmednagar, Pune, Nashik, Dhule, Aurangabad, Sholapur and Burhanpur; in -1300 'also reached north into the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh' (Navdatoli near Maheshwar)

ledger.note: c. 1400 BCE: the Jorwe culture appears in the Maharashtra Deccan. 'The early phase of the culture is dated to c. 1400-1000 BCE'; 'existed in large areas of the Deccan region in what is now Maharashtra state'. The year is the page's; the country is my reading of the named sites.

c. 1400 BCE: Daimabad and Inamgaon pass from the Malwa culture to the Jorwe. Both pages list the two sites; 'The Jorwe culture was preceded by the Malwa culture' (Jorwe page); the Malwa page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa_culture) has it 'succeeded by the Jorwe culture'.

region.text: the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh

ledger.note: c. 1300 BCE: the Jorwe culture reaches the Malwa plateau. The page says the culture 'also reached north into the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh' and lists Navdatoli near Maheshwar; the Malwa page ends 'c. 1300 BCE' ('mainly dated to c. 1600 - c. 1300 BCE'). No page dates the northward spread; -1300 is the end of the Malwa culture.

ledger.note: c. 700 BCE: the last Jorwe settlements are abandoned. 'Most Jorwe culture sites were abandoned around 1000 BCE ... after which the remaining sites show growing poverty until their abandonment around 700 BCE'; succeeded by 'the Iron Age megalithic culture of the Deccan and the Northern Black Polished Ware culture', which have no dossiers here.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture known from about 200 settlements; the page names no rivers or districts and the land abandoned around 1000 BCE is not placed.

sources.title: Jorwe culture

sources.title: Malwa culture
sources.note: Used for the handover: Malwa 'mainly dated to c. 1600 - c. 1300 BCE', succeeded by Jorwe.

notes: Type culture; no Cliopatria row; no area on the page. The Maharashtra discs are my reading of the named sites (Jorwe, Daimabad, Inamgaon, Prakashe, Walki), not a boundary; Khandesh below Dhule and Burhanpur is only partly covered. Contraction: the page says most sites were abandoned around 1000 BCE and the rest declined to 700; it does not say where, so no loss is written and the late shape equals the early one plus Malwa. Successors (the Iron Age megalithic culture of the Deccan, Northern Black Polished Ware) have no dossier. The pairing with the Malwa culture (Maharashtra -1400, plateau -1300) is bridging from the two pages' date ranges.
